title: Fortnite Explained | History, Battle Royale, Chapters and Modes | Gaming Explained
description: Fortnite explained: how Epic Games went from Save the World to Battle Royale, how a match works, chapters and seasons, concerts, Creative, UEFN, LEGO Fortnite and more.

sections.heading: What is Fortnite
sections.script: One hundred players jump from a flying bus, land on an island, grab weapons, build walls out of thin air and try to be the last one standing. That is Fortnite, the free game from Epic Games that became a pop culture phenomenon. But Fortnite is far more than one game now. It is a battle royale, a building sandbox, a place for concerts and a platform where players make their own worlds. In this explainer we cover how Fortnite started, how a quick idea turned into a global hit, how the game works, what the chapters and seasons are, the new modes like LEGO Fortnite, and where the game stands today. If you have ever wondered what everyone is talking about, you are in the right place.

sections.heading: A zombie game that changed course
sections.script: The story starts long before the hit. Epic Games first announced Fortnite in two thousand eleven as a cooperative game, a mix of building and survival where up to four players collect resources, build forts and defend them from monsters. Development took a long time, partly because the industry was moving toward games as a service, and Epic was also busy with other projects. That mode, called Save the World, finally arrived in early access in July of twenty seventeen. It was a decent success, but nobody expected what happened next. The team had a surprise waiting, and it came from watching another game take over the world.

sections.heading: The birth of Battle Royale
sections.script: In March of twenty seventeen, a game called PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds launched in early access and made the battle royale genre a worldwide hit. Epic's leaders saw the opportunity. Around the middle of the year, they decided to build their own battle royale mode on top of the Fortnite engine. The team made the mode in about two months, using existing assets from Save the World. Epic first planned to include it in the paid game, but two weeks before launch it chose to release it as a separate free game. Fortnite Battle Royale launched on September twenty sixth, twenty seventeen.

sections.heading: An explosive start
sections.script: The free price and the fast, colorful action worked. Epic said the mode passed ten million players in just two weeks, announced on October eleventh, twenty seventeen. In June of twenty eighteen, Epic announced more than one hundred twenty five million players, less than a year after launch. The same month, the game came to the Nintendo Switch, and it was available on consoles, PC and mobile, with the ability to play together across many platforms. By November of twenty eighteen, Fortnite had more than two hundred million registered accounts. Fortnite had gone from a side project to one of the biggest games in the world in just a few months, which is almost unheard of.

sections.heading: How a match works
sections.script: If you are new, here is how a match works. Up to one hundred players, alone or in squads, ride the Battle Bus across the island and jump out wherever they like. On the ground you have only a pickaxe, so you must find weapons, healing items and materials. A storm slowly shrinks the safe area, forcing everyone closer together. The signature feature is building: you can harvest wood, stone and metal from almost anything, and use it to create walls, ramps and floors to defend yourself or reach high ground. Later, Epic added a mode called Zero Build for players who prefer pure shooting, plus ranked play. In squad modes, a teammate who is knocked down can be revived, and since April of twenty nineteen even eliminated teammates can come back using Reboot Vans placed around the map. Winning your first match is a special moment, and the famous Victory Royale screen is the goal of every player. The game is free to play and earns money by selling cosmetics, such as outfits and emotes, for the in game currency called V-Bucks, plus a Battle Pass each season, which gives rewards as you earn experience.

sections.heading: Chapters and seasons
sections.script: Fortnite tells a story through its live updates. The game is divided into seasons that last about two or three months, and groups of seasons form chapters. In a new season, the map changes and new items, characters and a new Battle Pass arrive. In October of twenty nineteen, Chapter Two began with a brand new map, which Epic used as a fresh start for the whole game. Later chapters followed in twenty twenty one, twenty twenty two, twenty twenty three and December of twenty twenty four. The seventh chapter began at the end of November twenty twenty five. Fortnite has now run for seven chapters and more than forty seasons, and every season has its own theme, from superheroes to ancient legends to gaming icons.

sections.heading: Concerts and crossovers
sections.script: Fortnite also changed how games work with music and pop culture. In February of twenty nineteen, the DJ Marshmello played a concert inside the game, and more than ten million players attended. Later events featured artists like Travis Scott, Ariana Grande and Metallica, and some shows debuted new songs with spectacular visual effects. The game also hosted film previews and trailers, including for Star Wars and for a Christopher Nolan film. Crossovers became a core part of the game, with characters from movies, comics, anime and other video games joining the island. This blend of events and collaborations made Fortnite feel less like a game and more like a place where people hang out, a digital town square for millions of players around the world.

sections.heading: Creative and a platform
sections.script: Epic also gave players the tools to build their own experiences. Fortnite Creative launched in December of twenty eighteen, letting players spawn items on their own islands and make arenas, race courses and puzzle games. In March of twenty twenty three, Epic released Unreal Editor for Fortnite, or UEFN, a standalone editor that uses the power of Unreal Engine five. In October of twenty twenty three, the main menu was redesigned to show many kinds of experiences, similar to platforms like Roblox. In December of twenty twenty three, Epic launched three new games inside Fortnite: LEGO Fortnite, a survival crafting game made with the LEGO Group, Rocket Racing from the makers of Rocket League, and Fortnite Festival, a music game from Harmonix, the studio behind Rock Band. All three were free to play.

sections.heading: OG, Reload and the comeback modes
sections.script: Fortnite also learned to look back. In November of twenty twenty three, Epic brought back the original Chapter One map for a short season, and it was so popular that it came back as a permanent mode called Fortnite OG, with seasons rotating through the early days. Fortnite Reload arrived in June of twenty twenty four, with smaller maps, forty player matches and the chance to respawn. The game has also had legal drama. In August of twenty twenty, Epic and Apple clashed over payments, and Fortnite was removed from the Apple App Store. In April of twenty twenty five, a court ruled that Apple could not block third party storefronts or take fees from them, a major step in that long dispute.

sections.heading: Fortnite today and your turn
sections.script: Today Fortnite has become one of the longest running live games, with over forty seasons and many ways to play. Epic keeps adding new modes, creator made islands and big collaborations, and the game shows no sign of slowing down. Whether you jump in for a match, a concert, or to build with friends, there is something for almost everyone. Now we want to hear from you. When did you play Fortnite for the first time, and which chapter was your favorite? Are you more of a builder or a Zero Build player? Tell us in the comments. If you enjoyed this explainer, like the video and subscribe for more gaming videos. See you on the Battle Bus.
